I already had my reservations about the game when I found out it would be always online, no couch co-op, no career, no create a player etc. And after playing the two betas I concluded for the amount of content it wasn't worth MY $30. Its not that its expensive its the principle. I'm tired of buying games off potential. I want my games to be finished. So I stuck wit my guns and didn't buy it but I did get a free code from a live streamer on Tuesday. And even though its not a bad game its severely lacking. They've been working on this game for about 5yrs prior to getting the NBA license and u telling me that a KO Tournament is all they could think of? And one of the devs was a creative director at NBA Street? The blueprint is already there. I honestly think them getting that NBA license was a gift and a curse. It makes the game seem more legit but it killed the creativity and u can tell all their focus shifted into making the NBA players likeness as accurate as possible and meeting a deadline. Also they don't understand the corner they've put themselves in by making this live service and drip feeding content. Gamers are spoiled and impatient these days so if those updates aren't dripping like water they will get bored and go else where. Especially since there's already not a lot to do in the game as it is. Last but not least the devs change the minimum system requirements overnight. I've been playing this game since beta and at launch with no problems but today the game wouldn't load without crashing. Something told me to look at the system requirements and it went from requiring Nvidia GTX 1060 gpu to Nvidia GTA 1070. So now I cant play the game at all. If I didn't get the game for free I would be more furious. Imagine the people who did and now cant play because of this sneaky change. This is why I will always push for offline games.

THIS GAME IS NOT NBA STREET!!! That said, if you lower your expectations the game isn't bad. In the game's current state, only buy it on a sale. Its fun especially if you have friends to play with but outside of that this game is just half-baked. If you want this game because you think it'll remind you of NBA Street 1&2 era, you'll be sadly disappointed. The only things this game has in common with NBA Street is that it's arcade style, has street legends, Bobbito Garcia(OG announcer from NBA Street but it's like 33% as much dialogue from him while in a game) and a mechanic similar to Gamebreaker in a way but it's called In the Zone(ITZ) and it's character based with different bonuses. The game works ok as is but its just a mixture of things that should've been considered before releasing that make it seem like its still in development. (No campaign currently [which is fine, rumors say one's coming in 2027], no create your own player[huge miss in my opinion], no standard first to 21 pickup games its just randomized rulings each round and only tournament style.) It's easy to get into but hard to master unless you're using the most popular players at the moment like KD, Anthony Edwards, Lebron or Wemby. All of which however, are immediately available from the start. Tricks feel watered down and stealing feels like it happens just a little too often even if you're using the guard the ball function(left trigger). The street legend players are very solid in their own merit but not must have's either. I hope they add Clifford "Stretch" Monroe(OG Street legend from the first NBA Street game) at some point down the line with updates. Personally my biggest gripe is that there's no way to kick a random player from your team after a match; everything else I eventually learned to live with. Switching the game mode to Solos and having to reinvite your one friend instead of a deliberate kick function is just silly to not have at launch. This game isn't terrible but like I said its just half-baked. A few solid updates could definitely save this game's reputation I was just expecting more from the creators of NBA Street. TLDR: Watered down modern NBA Street, a 6.7/10 with potential to be MUCH better. Don't buy it at full price if you can resist the urge.

I think the negative reviews are coming from people comparing this to NBA Street Vol. 2 or because it's currently online-only. Honestly... I get it. That's what I thought I was buying too. That said, NBA The Run is its own game, it's way more technical than Street Vol. 2 was and I believe it has its own vibe going on. The movement is exactly how they advertised it; straight butter. Once you get the control down and play kinda like a real-life 3V3, everything clicks. Crossovers, give-and-gos, and step-back 3s all feel incredibly satisfying. (hit em with a Taunt after a bucket to increase competitiveness lol) My biggest complaints are the collision system and (for now) no ranked matchmaking. Sometimes you'll run into your own teammate, get launched into the backboard going for a rebound, or wonder if your teammates are playing with their controller upside down. 😂 I was disappointed about the online-only launch, but seeing the devs announced ranked in August, a campaign mode in 2027, and more players gives me hope. They actually want this game to be as good as it could be. Bobbito as the MC? Straight nostalgia. The soundtrack? lovin it. (Also... why'd y'all nerf the block sound effect? Run that volume back up :) Until ranked drops, matchmaking is all over the place. One game I'm with newbie players, the next I'm playing a squad that's apparently been training in the Hyperbolic Time Chamber since the playtest. 😂 Overall, this isn't NBA Street Vol. 2, and that's okay. Once I stopped expecting that, I started appreciating it for what it is. 9.5/10. Definitely recommend. @NBATHERUN... can I send you some beats? I've got a catalog of instrumentals & melodies just sitting on my hard drive waiting for their rookie contract. :)

I hate to say this as I reaaaaaallly wanted this game to be good / fun... and it was at first. But after playing for about 80 hours, the game just feels hollow and is losing the initial spark that made me look past a lot of it's deficits. There's a lot of game-changing bugs. And the balance is alllllllll over the place. Also without a dedicated 3 stack, it's brutal. Solo queuing is not for the faint of heart. Not even because of facing incredibly good opponents, but having incredibly dumb teammates / leavers. There's currently no penalty for leaving games and leaving your team high and dry. Not worth 30$. Prolly worth like 10$ in it's current state. Edit: They just did a big update where they didn't fix any glaring issues and added the top 3 drafts as the first character additions to the game....lol Also AJ Dybantsa is tied for 2nd highest stat distribution out of all characters. For example, Shai, Young Luka, LeBron, and Joker are all tied for 56 total stat points. AJ has 58 lol. He is straight up OP on release and he hasn't played a single NBA game yet. Their priorities are hard to read: the game has a serious issue with forfeit / leaving game abuse, poor AI performance for when a player does leave your team and is replaced with a bot, balancing issues (characters like wemby and aj are OP) which bleed further when you play a team of 2 wembys 1 aj for example. Right now, AJ, Giannis, Wemby, and El-Gigante are spammed. Part of the balancing issues are also mechanical: the current meta completely pushes out small guards. To continue, there's also only 3 game modes, and they're all the same, just slightly different in the way they queue: solos you play all 3 characters yourself, squads you play a single character on a team of 3, and friends you play in a bracket of friends grouped up together - but they are all ultimately the same "game mode." That said, there are different objectives round to round - but the point is it's getting monotonous. They did announce a "career mode" but that's set into 2027 I believe. The game also suffers from no real offline or practice mode where you can play against bots. All of that was to say: WOW! their first big update is such a let down. You release 3 characters that i don't think anyone really wanted since they're the most recent draft class - how about we put KAT or OG from the championship team? Or a legacy player like Jordan or Kobe? I understand they have to deal with licensing, but still.... I would've felt better about an update that actually fixes one of the many issues I mentioned, or expands on the games scope for different game modes to play. Even just releasing a real practice mode instead of shootaround would've been an improvement. TL:DR - This game is not worth it. I really want it to be, but it's not in it's current state - and with the direction the dev team has move so far, I don't anticipate it becoming worth it anytime soon if ever.
